title: prompt unit test harness (scratchpad)
content:
Elevator: developer-side harness for small, fast "unit" checks against prompts and response transforms. Run locally, in CI, or as preflight for rollouts. Not a replacement for large eval suites — cheap, deterministic cases for catching regressions in instructions, templates, and post-processing glue.

Why now (notes):
- We see frequent tiny regressions after model swaps (tone/formatting/metadata fields missing).
- E2E evals are slow/expensive; teams want quick feedback loops.
- Product folks keep hand-running small example prompts when changing templates -> brittle.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Author a set of small test cases (input -> expected assertions) that run in <3s per test on hosted sandbox.
- Integrate into CI to fail on obvious format regressions (missing JSON keys, wrong status strings, token-length explosion).
- Provide lightweight SDK + CLI so developers can run tests locally and gate PRs.
- Store tests with metadata (model pins, tolerance levels, tags) and surfaced in Console for teams.

Non-goals:
- Not doing human labels or subjective quality scoring — only deterministic checks and heuristics (regex, JSON schema, semantic similarity thresholds).
- Not replacing full eval pipelines or golden set A/B testing.

Test primitives (ideas):
- exact_match: expected string equality (for strict format pieces).
- json_schema: run response through simple JSON schema validator (required fields, types).
- contains: substring checks for required tokens (e.g., "Steps:").
- regex: flexible pattern checks for dates/IDs/etc.
- semantic_threshold: embedding-based similarity > X for short answers (for paraphrase-tolerant checks).
- token_count_max: guard against generation blowups.
- no_forbidden_phrases: safety/branding checks.

Example test (YAML-ish pseudocode):
- name: onboarding-email-format
  description: ensure assistant returns JSON object with `subject` and `body_html` keys
  model: gpt-4o-mini:2026-02-10  # pinned in test metadata
  prompt_template: onboarding/email-template.mustache
  input: {name: "Aisha", plan: "pro"}
  assertions:
    - json_schema: |
        required: [subject, body_html]
        properties:
          subject: {type: string}
          body_html: {type: string}
    - token_count_max: 1024
    - no_forbidden_phrases: ["internal-only", "do not send"]

API / UX sketch:
- CLI: redwood prompt-test run [path/to/test.yaml] --model=auto --compare:local
- SDK (python/js): TestCase object, run(), report() -> returns structured result (pass/fail + telemetry).
- Console: simple list with last-run status, history, last-run model, quick re-run button (sandbox or dedicated).
- Integrations: GitHub Actions orb, GitLab step, and pre-commit hook to run a small subset.

Execution modes + cost controls:
- local-fast: use small local runtime or sandbox mock that returns cached responses for stable mocks (dev-only).
- hosted-sandbox: short bursts against hosted models (use dev credits, limit tokens).
- smoke-ci: run only strict tests in CI (no embeddings/semantics) to keep cost low.
- nightly-eval: optional, run semantic tests and broader suites overnight.

Telemetry + diagnostics we need:
- test run duration, token counts, model used, region, error type (timeout, malformed output).
- diff output with golden (side-by-side in Console).
- heatmap of flaky tests (frequent intermittent failures).

Rollout strategy (rough):
1) internal alpha with dev-ex team: only CLI + python SDK + small tests.
2) invite 3 product teams (templates, email, chat) for wider alpha + CI integration.
3) Console integration + GitHub actions + billing quotas.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- CLI + python SDK available, docs with 3 example tests.
- CI action that can run a test subset under 2 minutes and fail PRs.
- Console shows last status for tests and allows re-run.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Semantic checks rely on embeddings (cost + drift). How to allow cheap local mocks? Option: support idealized golden stubs stored in repo and enable opt-in semantic mode.
- How strict to be for production gating? Some teams want strict formatting, others want fuzzier checks. Need per-test tolerance config.
- Where to store test artifacts and history? DB vs Git (prefer tests-as-code + Console pulls metadata). Need retention policy.
- Security: tests may send secrets in prompts. Add redaction + environment-aware mock mode.

Quick TODOs (next actions):
- [ ] spike CLI + runner prototype (Sam)
- [ ] design test YAML schema (Mika)
- [ ] run 5 example tests against email templates (Noelle)
- [ ] draft GH Action and a pre-commit hook (Evelyn)
- [ ] write short Console mockup (screenshots) for PM review

Random notes / rough ideas (brainstorming):
- Allow grouping tests into suites that map to product routes (e.g., onboarding-suite).
- "Golden snapshots" mode: store canonical responses (hashed) to detect token diffs. Could be toggled per-test.
- Auto-suggest fixes: when json_schema fails, attempt to run a sanitizer transformer (try to extract valid JSON) and present suggestion.
- Quick lint: run prompts through a linter to catch obvious missing fields before hitting model.
- Support parameterized tests (table-driven) to exercise variations without duplicating files.

Notes to self: keep interfaces tiny to start. focus on missing-key regressions and token spikes — 70% of the pain. Resist adding heavy eval features in MVP.

End of scratchpad (will iterate).
